web.description: A how-to guide for Stimulus: tones, sweeps with hold and scrub, harmonics with subharmonics, noise colours and band limiting, polarity pulses, mixing up to four generators, and exporting test files.
web.ogDescription: What each generator does and how to use it: tone, sweep, harmonics, noise, polarity, the mixer, master section and export.

cta.title: Stimulus
cta.text: A signal generator for live sound: tones, sweeps, harmonics, noise and polarity pulses, mixed across four generators.

intro.text: Stimulus generates test signals for PA tuning and audio work: steady tones, sweeps you can hold and scrub, harmonic stacks, six noise colours with band limiting, and polarity pulses. Up to four generators run at once through a small mixer with a safety limiter on the output.

blocks.text: The editor shows one generator at a time; the rack on the right holds them all. Click a strip to edit it, press **Add** to spawn another (up to four), and the cross on a strip removes it. Each strip has its own level fader plus **M** (mute), **S** (solo) and the polarity flip.
Each generator can be a different type - run a tone against a sweep, or two tones for dual-tone tests. The transport at the bottom right starts and stops everything together.

Type a frequency or use the slider. The **Min** and **Max** fields set the slider's range: narrow them (say 400 to 500) and the full slider travel covers just that span, giving 1 Hz precision when you need it. The full range is 10 Hz to 22 kHz, always clamped to what your output device can actually reproduce.

Null and cancellation tests: two tones at the same frequency with one polarity flipped cancel exactly when their phases are aligned. Phases align at Play, so set your frequencies first and then press **Play**. If you move a frequency while running, that generator's phase drifts relative to the others (the price of click-free frequency glides) - tap **Play** again to restart from the top and re-align.

Set the range by typing **Start** and **End** or by dragging the two thumbs on the range slider - the ringed thumb is the end. Crossing the thumbs (or the swap button) gives a down sweep. Sweeps run log or linear over the set duration.

items: **Return** sweeps to the end frequency and back to the start, with a seamless turnaround.
**Loop** repeats the sweep until you stop it.
**CONT/STEP** switches to stepped mode: the sweep dwells on each 1/3-octave frequency for the set dwell time, including the end frequency.

blocks.text: While a sweep runs, **HOLD** freezes it at the frequency on screen and keeps it sounding as a steady tone. A bright thumb appears on the range slider - drag it (or use the arrow keys) to move the held tone anywhere in the sweep range. Resume continues the sweep from wherever you left it.
**Pause** freezes the position and silences the audio; pause again to resume in place. **Play** always restarts from the top, even out of hold or pause - tap it repeatedly to retrigger a sweep.

A fundamental with subharmonics below it and harmonics above: f/4, f/3, f/2, the fundamental, then 2f to 5f, each on its own fader. The label under each fader shows the actual frequency it lands on; a dash means that partial falls outside the playable range and stays silent. Everything is phase-locked to the fundamental.

Six colours, ordered by slope: **Red/Brown** (-6 dB per octave), **Pink** (-3), **White** (flat), **Grey** (perceptually flat), **Blue** (+3) and **Violet** (+6). Pink is the usual choice for PA work; red/brown is the same signal Smaart calls red.
**Band limit** restricts any colour to one octave or 1/3 octave around a centre frequency - set the centre with the frequency controls that appear. Band-limited pink on a sub is the classic use.

A positive-going pulse at a set interval for polarity checks. **FULL** is the standard 4 ms pulse; **SUB** stretches it to 20 ms so it reads clearly through subwoofers. The first movement is always positive - if your tester or ears say otherwise, something in the chain is flipped.

Each generator has a level fader, fade in/out times, and an **Output** switch: left channel, right channel, or both (dual mono - no centre dip). The master section has its own fader, always-visible meters, and a safety limiter, on by default at -3 dBFS, that hard-clips rather than letting four summed generators overshoot.
New generators always start at -20 dBFS. Nothing in Stimulus ever defaults to full scale.
The Presets menu recalls factory setups (1 kHz tone, pink noise, full-range sweep, sub sweep, sub drop) and saves your own - a preset captures every generator plus the master section.

Export renders the current setup to a WAV or AIFF file - 44.1, 48 or 96 kHz at 16, 24 or 32-bit float - for any length you set, named after what it contains. Files start and end with a 10 ms fade so they never click, and renders are deterministic: the same setup produces the same file every time.

items: **Return** - play, or restart from the top while running
**Left/Right arrows** - nudge the frequency (or scrub a held sweep) by 1%; add **Shift** for 10%
